latest.title: Appointment of Chief Financial Officer
latest.content:
20 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 3957R
IG Design Group PLC
20 August 2026
20 August 2026
IG Design Group plc
("the Company", "the Group" or "Design Group")
Appointment of Chief Financial Officer
IG Design Group plc, a leading designer, innovator and manufacturer across various celebration and creative categories, today announces that Rohan Cummings will step down as Chief Financial Officer ("CFO") and from the Board with effect from 31 August 2026. The Board is pleased to announce the appointment of Ari Bensoussan as its new CFO, effective from 1 September 2026. Ari will also join the Board as an executive director with effect from that date.
Ari has nearly 30 years' experience across finance, strategy and M&A in global consumer businesses. He joins from Thai Union Group PCL, a global seafood leader, where he has served as Chief Financial Officer, Europe since 2021. Prior to this, Ari spent almost 25 years at Nestlé, holding a number of senior roles including Head of Finance and Group Controller at Nestlé Waters as well as Head of Operations Strategy and Mergers and Acquisitions Director for the Nestlé Group.
Rohan will continue to support the Company through to 31 December 2026 to ensure an orderly handover.
Stewart Gilliland, Non-Executive Chair, commented:
"On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank Rohan for his significant contribution to the Company over the past three years. He has played an important role during a period of significant change for the Group, including the successful disposal of DG Americas, which marked a major step in reshaping and simplifying the business and renegotiating the Group's banking facilities. His contribution has helped position Design Group as a focused business with a robust balance sheet and strong foundations for its next phase. We wish him every success in the future.
"I am delighted to welcome Ari to the Board. His extensive international finance and commercial experience will be hugely valuable as we look to broaden our customer reach and strengthen our commercial capabilities, while maintaining the financial discipline that has underpinned the Group's recent progress."

Notes to Editors:
IG Design Group plc is one of the world's leading designers, innovators and manufacturers of gift packaging, greeting cards, stationery, creative play products and related items. The Group designs, sources and manufactures a broad portfolio of products across multiple categories and occasions, encompassing every day, seasonal and celebration ranges.
The Group operates across key international markets, with a strong presence in the United Kingdom, Europe and Australia. Its products are sold to a diverse customer base including major retailers and supermarkets such as Tesco, Costco and Aldi, as well as discounters, online platforms and independent stores. The Group's heritage brand, Tom Smith, holds a Royal Warrant for the supply of Christmas crackers and Christmas wrapping paper to the Royal Family, a distinction it has held continuously since 1906.
Across IG Design Group's global teams, it manages a portfolio of more than 22,000 SKUs, supplying over 550 million units annually to customers in approximately 70 countries. The Group operates a vertically integrated model, combining in
‑
house design expertise with global sourcing, manufacturing, distribution and fulfilment capabilities. Its manufacturing footprint includes three facilities located in Wales, the Netherlands and Poland. This integrated platform enables the Group to deliver innovative, responsibly sourced products at scale, while maintaining cost efficiency, speed to market and flexibility.
IG Design Group plc is listed on the AIM market of the London Stock Exchange.

company_30s.what_they_do: IG Design Group is a specialist in creating digital user‑experience solutions for the automotive, aviation and industrial sectors. They build software platforms that help manufacturers design, simulate and manufacture components, and provide consulting services to optimise production workflows.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The global shift to connected, autonomous vehicles and smart manufacturing creates a huge addressable market. IG Design’s tools enable companies to reduce design time, cut prototyping costs and accelerate time‑to‑market, giving them a competitive edge in a high‑growth industry.
company_30s.current_state: IG Design has just finished its 2025 annual report. The company is generating revenue but is still in a high‑cash‑burn phase, relying on capital raises and share buybacks to fund growth. Its shares have slid sharply, trading near the lower edge of their 52‑week range.

rns_narrative: The latest filings show a steady stream of corporate actions: new shares are being issued, the board is increasing its own holdings, and a share‑buyback programme is underway. These moves signal that insiders believe the stock is undervalued and are willing to invest more capital.

Financially, the company posted its full‑year results and a grant of long‑term incentive payments. The earnings release hints at a turnaround in profitability, while the buyback and director share‑acquisition events reinforce confidence.
Collectively, the narrative is one of a company that is stabilising its balance sheet, reinforcing its leadership position, and signalling that the market may soon recognise its value.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism – traders are listening for a breakout, but no one is shouting about it.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bullish voices highlight a recent profitable day and the fact that insiders are buying more shares. They expect a rebound once the market recognises the company’s improved fundamentals.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bearish chatter is minimal; the few negative posts point to a lack of momentum and concern that the share‑buyback may not be enough to lift the price.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The tone has shifted from indifferent to cautiously hopeful. The community is waiting for a clear catalyst before committing capital.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends are flat – there is no public buzz. A silent market is a prime spot for a surprise rally when a catalyst arrives.

near_term_catalysts: A formal announcement of the completion of the share‑buyback programme – the company will need to disclose the total amount repurchased, which could trigger a price lift.
The next quarterly earnings report (expected in early September). If earnings beat expectations and revenue growth is stronger than last year, it would provide a strong bullish signal.
A new partnership or contract win in the automotive or aviation sector. Any announcement that expands the client base or locks in long‑term revenue would reinforce the turnaround story.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden spike in daily volume that exceeds 1.5× the average, a price bounce above the 20‑day moving average, and a bullish candlestick pattern at the 52‑week low.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is still in the early phase of a deep crash. The APEX score suggests a tight compression, meaning the next move could be sharp. Confirmation will come when volume surges and the price clears the 20‑day moving average while insiders continue to buy.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The company’s insiders are buying more shares, the board is buying back stock, and earnings have improved – classic signs of a turnaround. If the price climbs to the middle of its 52‑week range, the upside is roughly 100% from the current level, giving a 2:1 risk‑reward ratio.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the buyback stalls or the earnings miss expectations, the price could stay near the bottom of the 52‑week range for months. The worst case is a further 10‑15% decline before a rebound, which would still be a loss if you entered at the current price.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: up to 10% if the price stays flat. Potential gain: double the current price if it recovers to the midpoint of the 52‑week band. The asymmetry is clear – the upside far outweighs the downside.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a break above the 20‑day moving average with volume at least 1.5× the average. Size the position so that a 10% drop would wipe out no more than 20% of the trade. Set a stop 5% below the entry to protect against a false breakout.
playbook.if_watching: Hold until the earnings report or the buyback completion is announced. If the price stays below the 20‑day moving average for more than 3 weeks, consider tightening the stop or exiting.
playbook.if_passing: None identified. No delisting, bankruptcy or fraud signals are present.

ai_insights.bottom_line: IG Design’s deep crash has been followed by insider buying and a share‑buyback – a rare combination that points to a potential 100% upside once the market recognises the turnaround, but the next move will hinge on the upcoming earnings and buyback confirmation.
